Contract:
`FeasibilityState` is not model memory. It is the fold of append-only `sdd-scaffold-feasibility/v1` JSON events in the compatible session's `journal:` section. The router has already proved/opened that session before scaffold starts, so the state survives an operator pause, context loss, and same-session resume without writing a second project artifact.
Each event is one compact UTF-8 JSON line with keys in this order: `schema`, `cycle`, `seq`, `event`, `payload`. `cycle` binds the scaffold target-set and initial ticket hashes; `seq` increases by one. Event kinds are: `opened` (target paths/hashes, worker session, `fallbackUsed=false`, `resultCount=0`, `activeCap=5`) · `target-refreshed` (latest paths/hashes and changed tickets) · `worker-state` · `sensor-result` (the NEW cumulative result count, literal verdict, literal Changes, and latest target hashes) · `operator-disposition` (the referenced result count and exact CLEAN / CONTINUE THROUGH ROUND N / RESTART answer) · `gate2-choice` · `closed`.
Before the first critic dispatch, append `opened`. After every ticket mutation, append `target-refreshed` before dispatch. Most importantly, after a critic returns, append the complete `sensor-result` with the already-incremented count and require tool success BEFORE interpreting CLEAN, a product fork, GOAL, the cap, or emitting any Ask. An operator answer is a separate later immutable `operator-disposition`; never rewrite the result it disposes. On resume, fold only the matching cycle's events. A latest `sensor-result` with no disposition and a cap/GOAL Ask pending means re-present that same decision from the recorded bytes — do not redispatch, increment, or reset. `activeCap` starts at exactly 5 and changes only by a recorded CONTINUE disposition.
To append any event, write that one JSON line to the regular non-symlink `.claude/tmp/sdd-scaffold-feasibility-event.json`, then execute the current scaffold transition's exact feasibility-event ToolCall. The successful command consumes the payload; inline event text is forbidden. `closed` is the explicit cleanup marker after STEP_5 integrity succeeds (or before an operator-confirmed RESTART opens a new cycle); the session scratch itself is removed only by its normal terminal `sdd-session close`.
